request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's own figures when a person on the sheet has the user's name
(by name or alias, as names are compared): that person's due-total and overdue-total; nothing when
there is no such person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's own figures when a person on the sheet has the user's name
(by name or alias, as names are compared): that person's due-total and overdue-total; nothing when

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows your own figures. When someone on the sheet has your signed-in name, either as their name or as one of their aliases, it shows that person's due-total and overdue-total. When no one matches, both fields are blank. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **Header** (`features/header/header.ts`): added "My due total" (`my-due-total`) and "My overdue total" (`my-overdue-total`) after the sheet's own totals.
- **Matching and figures** (`features/people/people.ts`): names match the way the server compares them, ignoring case and spaces at either end. A match on a person's name wins over a match on someone's alias. The two figures come from the same calculation as the due-total and overdue-total columns on that person's row, so the header always agrees with the row, including after a hold or a cap.

This was a front-end change only. The page already loads every person with their aliases and the data the totals are worked out from, so the server and stored data didn't need to change. Retired people count as a match too, the same way the people count in the header includes them.
